Subject: Operational redundancy claims — RTO/RPO logs and owner matrix request

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the overview last week. As part of Silverline's risk review for the payments integration, our security team has a few follow-ups related to your BCP/DR assertions:

1) You state a 15-minute RTO for the hosted inference API for single-region failover in the SOC narrative. Can you provide the actual runbook step timestamps (what triggers the failover, who executes, time-to-first-successful-request) from a recent exercise? We want machine-readable traces or logs if available.

2) For multi-region failover, please share the ownership matrix — which Redwood teams execute which steps during failover, and fallback order for compatible model variants.

3) Any artifacts demonstrating KV-cache warm start times or prefix-cache priming scripts you run during warm standby?

If you can share a short package (logs + a one-page summary) we can close this line in our SIG questionnaire. We need this by COB Tue (2026-10-12) to stay on schedule.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Cheers,
Olivia Barnes
Security Operations Manager
Silverline Payments

Subject: Re: Operational redundancy claims — RTO/RPO logs and owner matrix request

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear asks. High level response below and we'll attach the artifacts you requested.

- Single-region failover (15 min RTO) — summary: Our internal warm-standby playbook runs an automated health probe sweep, then triggers the routing policy swap. Measured time-to-first-successful-request in the July 2026 tabletop was 12m 48s (see attached warm-failover-trace.log). The runbook includes the scripted KV-cache replay; warm priming reduced cold-token latency by ~40% in the test.

- Multi-region failover ownership matrix — attached runbook-ownership-matrix.xlsx. Key owners:
  * Infra Oncall (infra@redwood.com) — routing / load-balancer policy
  * Runtime Team (runtime@redwood.com) — kernel selection & quantization fallback
  * Platform Ops (platform@redwood.com) — cache priming and upstream routing TTLs

- KV-cache warm start artifacts — included scripts and timing traces in rto-rpo-summary-20261009.pdf; warm-failover-trace.log contains individual request timings and cache hit evolution.

We don't expose customer data in the traces — logs are redacted for PII and include request timestamps, errors, and cache metrics.

I've uploaded a short package to a shared folder (link below) and attached the three files to this thread. If you'd like a live walkthrough, Marissa and Ben are on this thread and can lead a 30-minute demo + Q&A.

Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bDRPlaybook

Best,
Alex Martinez

alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Also, Silverline security would like to schedule a short witness session where Redwood runs the same failover path in a staging window while our DevOps watches the metrics and signs an acceptance note. From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Operational redundancy claims — RTO/RPO logs and owner matrix request

Hi Olivia — appreciate the careful read. Short answers and proposed next steps: 

1) Orchestration trigger: our probe is named "service-health-check-v2" (threshold: 3 consecutive failed probes over 60s window). When threshold met, the routing controller marks the node unhealthy and routing policy swaps to standby targets. The retry pattern you observed is expected during an LB drain window — we attempt in-flight retries for up to 300s to allow graceful handoff, which explains the earlier requests you saw. I've added a highlighted notes section in the one-pager (rto-rpo-summary-20261009.pdf) that calls this out explicitly.

2) Witness session: Thu 10/15 14:00-15:00 PT works on our side. We'll run the staged failover in our staging region with Ben leading the runbook and Alex presenting the metrics. We'll invite you to the shared console and stream the relevant logs. Please confirm attendee emails and whether you need a non-disclosure addendum for the live traces.

Deliverables before session (we'll send by Wed COB): updated one-pager with probe names and timing callouts, sanitized trace excerpts, and a playbook excerpt showing the exact CLI commands we run.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
